low-score-fixtures.ts binds seed 8241 and content 0.1.0 to expert, incomplete-care, recovery, and no-action contrasts. No infection, host-response, or treatment model is claimed.

low-score.ts runs two authored transitions. The family states its concern more plainly at 20 minutes, with the observations and the score unchanged. The requested medical review arrives 90 minutes after it is requested, confirms that treatment was warranted at the time of the call, and reports that the score at that moment was still 2. Nothing arrives unrequested, because the failure being taught is that nobody called. The observations deliberately never drift: a rising score would trigger the threshold and turn this into an ordinary escalation drill.

The learner records the observations with the score as calculated, records what the score does and does not exclude, records the family report in its own words rather than converting it to a number, requests review on recorded concern rather than on a threshold, reviews the boundaries, and arranges increased observation. Deferring because the score is low, excluding infection on a normal temperature, substituting a more specific screening tool, and documenting without calling are each refused.

Recorded observations, recorded exclusions, the family report, escalation on concern, the boundary review, increased observation, and a current full assessment permit handoff with the diagnosis open. lost-contingency.ts runs two authored transitions. At 12 minutes the hourly urine output is reported at 35 millilitres, above the threshold the written plan names and for one hour rather than two, so nothing is triggered; what it does is make the plan matter. If the reconstructed plan is taken to the surgical registrar, they confirm 18 minutes later that it stands as written, unchanged. The patient does not deteriorate, because a decline would let a learner treat the decline as the reason the plan mattered when the point is that it mattered before.

The learner records what was said, reads the notes, records the difference as a transmission gap rather than a documentation gap, reconstructs the contingency in the surgical team’s words, states what the gap changed, takes the plan to be confirmed, reviews the boundaries, and keeps the observations against the named threshold. Treating an unmentioned plan as absent, telephoning the day nurse to recall what she omitted, reading a short handover as a straightforward patient, and authoring a replacement plan are each refused. Recording the gap before both sources are read, reconstructing before the gap is recorded, and requesting confirmation before there is a reconstructed plan are refused as premature.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.
